title: Veterans find a new mission with senior dogs
description: Veterans working with Frankie and Andy's place, a shelter for senior dogs in Winder, Ga., have found a new mission for both themselves and senior dogs by bringing joy to people in the community.

transcript.text: - [Narrator] The word veteran tends to evoke images
of troops serving in the military.
At Frankie and Andy's Place, a shelter for senior dogs
in Winder, Georgia, military veterans are helping
veterans of another kind, dogs who are all survivors
of abuse and neglect.
Together, the dogs and the veterans have a new mission,
of bringing companionship to people in the community.
The veterans bring both unique skills and unique attitudes,
and their sense of teamwork and organization
make them a welcome addition to the program
for both the dogs and the staff.
- It doesn't matter if it's torrential rain.
Ah, not a problem.
Tornado coming through, I'm still there.
That's what that's brought to this.
It's a never say die, let's get it done, we've got
a job to do, let's get out there and just teach
the world what these senior dogs have got.
The veterans that are involved in this program,
that's basically what all of them bring to this.
- [Narrator] For Vietnam veteran Linda Wick,
it's a mutually beneficial relationship for both
her and the dogs.
They give and receive love and support from each other,
while doing the same for seniors in their community.
It's a chance to show that no matter their age,
the dogs can impact others with just a touch.
- The program is wonderful.
Too many people today want to just dispose of dogs
when they get too old.
But, senior dogs have so much to offer.
The people just don't want to take the time to see.
- [Narrator] Whether on two legs or four,
all of these veterans are working together to show
the world that they're making a positive difference
in the lives of others.
From Winder, Georgia, I'm Army Staff Sergeant
Lisa Rodriguez-Presley.
(laughter)
